- Selection at 95% (E048) cut 0.35 s (−6.3%). Its 3-seed reading was −0.14 pp, which is noise-level, so its rate is about 2.5 s/pp or better but unproven.

- Systems trims (I076) are about 1% and free in accuracy, so they are worth stacking but do not decide anything alone.
- The PCIe judge adds about 5–10% to absolute time. Bandwidth-bound savings may shrink slightly there.

W3 (cost lens), after E048.

**Tip (E036, 60645dd).** 231 steps at batch 2000. Resolution is 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30% of steps. The whitening is detached from 20% and the stem is frozen from 75%. Eight math-identical reruns timed 5.29–5.34 s, so time reproduces to about 1%.

**Accuracy and noise.**
- Seeds 0–2 on the tip and its math-identical copies read 0.7532, 0.7525, 0.7497, 0.7519, 0.7520 and 0.7544, a mean of about 0.7523.
- Rebuild autotuning moves the 3-seed mean by about ±0.25 pp. The population mean is about 0.7525–0.7535.
- A null change passes the 0.753 gate about 35–40% of the time.
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp and the 20-seed SE about 0.07 pp. Only same-build 20-seed pairings carry signal.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s fixed + Σ steps × per-step cost.
- Per step: 32 px 0.032 s, 28 px 0.026 s, 24 px 0.021 s, 20 px 0.016 s. The average step costs about 0.021 s, so 6 steps add about 0.125 s.
- Whitening detach saves about 8% of a step and the stem freeze about 27%. A group-2 freeze on top saves about 0.010 s per frozen step (E046: −0.236 s over 23 steps).
- Truncation is worth more than its FLOP share because it also skips memory-bound BN/GELU backward, the optimizer and Lookahead traffic (H6.6, my E046 time miss).
- Non-step GPU work is about 135 ms (E047). I expect at most about half of it can be removed without changing any number.
- Selection at 95% (E048) cut 0.35 s (−6.3%). Its 3-seed reading was −0.14 pp, which is noise-level, so its rate is about 2.5 s/pp or better but unproven.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: about 1–2.5. Freeze at 75%: about 2. Freeze at 60%: a cliff at about 0.65. Width: about 0.7.
- Selection: about 2.3 (E031); E048 is ambiguous.
- Group-2 freeze: its held-out cost is still unknown. If it is ≤0.12 pp, it is the best lever left.

**Funders.** All six boosters tested so far read ≤0 (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045). My prior for a new booster is −0.05 ± 0.2 pp. Accuracy has to be bought with steps, and the cheapest steps are frozen 32 px steps.

**Mechanisms**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is near its optimum.
2. The late 28/32 px phases and a stem that trains until about 70–75% carry accuracy (E018, E024, E037, E040, E041).
3. Early accuracy depends on step count and the LR schedule, not on pixels (E026, E033, E045).
4. Backward truncation is the dominant cheap time lever, and its cost is set by the anneal window (E028, E036, E046).
5. Muon renormalizes filters every step, so filter weight decay has no effect.
6. airbench chose GELU over ReLU for accuracy. On a bytes-bound fused step, ReLU saves little time (its mask is still a read and write) and probably costs 0.2–0.5 pp. That is a poor exchange rate.

**Strategy**
- Cascade plus top-up (I075) is the main candidate.
- Systems trims (I076) are about 1% and free in accuracy, so they are worth stacking but do not decide anything alone.
- The PCIe judge adds about 5–10% to absolute time. Bandwidth-bound savings may shrink slightly there.

**Unsure**
- The group-2 freeze's held-out delta.
- How many of the 68 ms of copies are cudagraph copy-ins that can be removed.
- Whether selection at 95% is actually cheap on held-out seeds.

forecasts.reason: The 6 extra steps add about 0.12 s to E046's 5.08 s, which puts it about 2% below E036, right at the decision threshold. The +0.25-epoch top-up roughly cancels a group-2 freeze cost of about 0.1 pp, and a 20-seed SE of about 0.07 pp cannot resolve a 0.03 pp criterion.
It can remove at most about 50–80 ms of the 135 ms, a saving of about 1%, which is the size of the time noise. Accuracy stays at the tip's level up to rebuild noise.

The fused kernels are bytes-bound, so ReLU saves only about 1–2% (an fp16 output or mask is still stored and read), while dropping GELU costs about 0.2–0.4 pp. Both of the hypothesis's thresholds fail.

cruxes: What is the group-2 freeze's same-build 20-seed accuracy cost? If it is ≤0.1 pp, the freeze cascade plus top-up becomes the base for every further cut. If it is ≥0.2 pp, only the epoch dial and systems trims are left.
How much of E047's 68 ms of copies is cudagraph copy-in or layout conversion that can be removed? That sets whether I076 saves 1% or nearly nothing.
Does 95% loss-based selection (E048: −6.3% time) hold within about 0.1 pp on held-out seeds 13–32? If it does, selection beats the dial and stacks with the freeze.
